Matt: I have an excellent business idea. I want to invest in the hardware and software industries. Do you have any advice?
Regina: You need to choose only one industry.
Matt: Why? Aren't they related?
Regina: Yes, they are, but the hardware industry is very different from the software industry. Although they have always coexisted, they don't have the same characteristics. You know that hardware is about the production and manufacturing of computer devices, right? Well, it has a high cost of entry, so only some largish and wealthy companies can develop hardware. On the other hand, I consider software succeeds out of effort and great knowledge of different programming languages. If you work with software, you won't have any big issues as long as there is enough individual determination.
Matt: In that case, I choose software.
Regina: I think it's the best option. Nowadays, big companies need software developments to improve quality in their processes. Software impacts global economy every day, think about the impact of the GPS technology.

Matt: You're right. Software covers many interesting purposes. I know that in finances you need to use some software; word processors and spreadsheets are some examples of that. There isn't any serious company that doesn't use those software tools. We can also use software to develop games and applications, which become very popular in a short time. That's a huge business advantage.
Regina: Of course! Software has low costs of entry and you reach clients easier than working with hardware. I mean, hardware is very important too because you need computer devices to develop software, but investing in software is a better option for you.

Matt: I know. I don't want to invest in something that may have a dead end. Thank you.
Regina: You're welcome! Remember that hardware or software are both challenging industries. But, if you ask me, the real history of technology starts with software.

Simple Present Tense in Affirmative and Negative Statements
You use simple present in affirmative and negative statements to talk about frequent actions and routines in the present.

For affirmative statements, we are going to follow the next structure:

Subject + verb + complement

Let's take a look at the following example:

Hardware and software work hand in hand.

Now, when you write an affirmative statement in simple present using thethird person of the singular, you need to add an –s, –es, or –ies at the end of the sentence:

The company works on software development.

In negative statements, we follow the next structure:

Subject + auxiliary verb in negative (don't / do not or doesn't/ does not) + verb (base form)+ complement

Let's see an example:

Hardware and Software industries do not focus on the same projects.

When you use the third person of the singular in a negative statement, you do not need to add the –s ( or –es) at the end because the auxiliary is already there. For example:

She does not work in the hardware industry.

Some and Any
You use some and any to measure countable and uncountable nouns.
I know that some software are for financial use where we use word processors and spreadsheets.

We use some when we talk in affirmative sentences and it describes an unspecified quantity. It means few (for countable nouns) or little (for uncountable nouns).

Example: I know how some hardware devices work.

We can also use some in questions for offering something.

Example: Would you like to know some information about the software industry?

On the other hand, you use any in negative statements for countable and uncountable nouns.

Example: She doesn't know any national company that works in the hardware industry.

We can also use any for questions.

Example: Is there any great advance in software development?
Do you have any advice?
